headline: OpenAI is reportedly in talks to let an unnamed film-industry startup use and modify its shelved Sora video model, months after closing it down.
score_reason: Pool score 5 lowered 1: first reported on 12 Oct (before the window) and resting on one unnamed source.
importance_line: Filmmakers could get a professional version of Sora while ordinary users may not get it back, but the talks are unconfirmed, rest on one unnamed source, and neither the startup's name nor the terms are known.
summary: The Information reported on 12 Oct 2026, as relayed by Digit and PYMNTS, that OpenAI is in talks, according to one person with knowledge of them, with an unnamed startup that wants access to Sora to modify it and sell software and services to filmmakers; the startup was co-founded by the Hollywood producer Jeffrey Katzenberg, Bill Peebles, who led Sora's research at OpenAI, and Sujay Jaswa, a former chief financial officer of Dropbox. It is unclear whether OpenAI would hand over Sora's weights (its trained settings), the talks are unconfirmed, and Digit reads a deal as making Sora mainly a professional tool rather than a service for everyone.
notes: Pool source Inshorts is a copy site relaying Digit, which relays The Information; the original is credited. Outlets differ on when Sora was shut (March vs April 2026), so the entry says only that it was closed earlier this year. Re-reported on 13 Oct 2026 without new facts that we could find; first reported 12 Oct 2026.
